meta.title: Ventana Lunar · When can you land at the lunar south pole?
meta.description: Pick any point near the lunar south pole and any hour: Ventana Lunar tells you when a lander has the Sun for power and the Earth in sight, and which Deep Space Network antenna is listening.
nav.label: Sections
hero.eyebrow: NASA Space Apps 2026 · Lunar Landing Site Navigator
hero.lede: Pick any point near the lunar south pole and any hour. Ventana Lunar tells you when a lander has both: the landing window, and which antenna on Earth is listening.
hero.moonAlt: The Moon lit from the east by a low Sun, its south pole in the lower half
live.label: IM-2 Athena right now
live.overRidge: {deg}° below the level, over the ridge
live.noListening: No antenna can hear the Moon now
live.noLink: No link: the Earth is out of sight · {station} would listen
live.noLinkNone: No link: the Earth is out of sight
live.computed: Computed in your browser by Ventana Lunar's own sky, read against the site's LOLA horizon.
how.title: Three choices. One answer you can read in five seconds.
how.placeBody: 29 landing sites, from Apollo to the Artemis candidates, or drop a pin anywhere on the Moon.
how.timeBody: Live on the clock, or scrub and play through the month hour by hour.
how.answerBody: Four colours, one meaning each, everywhere in the app.
month.title: {month} at IM-2 Athena
month.caption: At the south pole the Sun circles the horizon and the Earth rises and sets with the Moon's wobble. Where both are up, a lander can work and talk: {share} of this month.
month.alt: {month} at IM-2 Athena: the Sun is up {sun} of the month, the Earth {earth}, both {window}.
science.title: Checked against JPL. Shaped by the real terrain.
science.accuracyBody: Our own sky against JPL Horizons, hour by hour, November and December 2026.
science.reliefBody: LOLA relief around each site: a ridge can hide a Sun that is still up.
science.dsnBody: Deep Space Network antennas: Goldstone, Canberra and Robledo de Chavela.
science.shadowBody: Sites in permanent shadow, flagged from NASA's illumination maps.
science.sources: Sources: JPL Horizons · LRO LOLA and LROC WAC · Mazarico et al. 2011 · NASA Blue Marble · Natural Earth
tour.title: Pick a site and a moment. Every view answers for it.
tour.lead: Change the site or the hour in one view and the others follow. Here all four show IM-2 Athena on 22 November 2026 at 20:00 UTC, a landing window.
tour.globeBody: The Moon lit as it is at that hour. Pick one of 29 sites or drop a pin anywhere.
tour.globeAlt: The app's globe view with IM-2 Athena selected and its landing window open
tour.footBody: The real relief around the point in 3D, out to 128 km, and the ridge that hides the Sun.
tour.footAlt: The app's 3D view standing at IM-2, the Sun and the Earth over a low ridge
tour.dsnBody: Which of NASA's three big antennas hears the lander, and when it hands over.
tour.dsnAlt: The app's DSN view with Robledo de Chavela listening
tour.phoneBody: Install it and use it offline with the last data, in five languages.
tour.phoneAlt: The app on a phone, the globe above and the site's widgets below
